unresolved_must_fix.claim: The revision cut the sentence naming Minister Adams's quiet manner, which was the antecedent of 'him'. 'They chose to ignore him, since they could not ridicule him' now directly follows '...except Sumner'.
unresolved_must_fix.counterevidence: The next sentences say 'Personally the Minister was to be kindly treated', which lets an attentive reader recover the referent.

evidence.quote: unassailable social position of Minister Adams in no way conciliated
all the Republican leaders except Sumner. They chose to ignore him, since they could not ridicule him.
The exceedingly quiet manner and the unassailable social position of Minister Adams in no way conciliated them.

unresolved_must_fix.minimal_repair: Restore 'The exceedingly quiet manner and the unassailable social position of Minister Adams in no way conciliated them.' before 'They chose to ignore him'.
unresolved_must_fix.plan_relation: required (British prejudice and the Minister's slow acceptance)
unresolved_must_fix.reader_effect: Readers may take Sumner as the one British society ignored, muddling who was snubbed and why. The point is that the Minister's unassailable position made him unridiculable.
unresolved_must_fix.title: 'Ignore him' now points to Sumner, not the Minister

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'nervous as wild beasts under the long strain' and the 'order of departure' clause partially explain the outburst.

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The 1778 voyage and the 'eighteenth century' idea of diplomacy remain.

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Para 22 ends with the expectation that 'Minister Adams would vanish with the rest', which partly primes the term.

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Retrospect survives later ('long leisure of later life', 'next thirty years'), and 'no friend in the Senate' in para 4 partly carries the Sumner point.
